DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)

The combination of a new headache, progressive vision loss, jaw claudication, and scalp tenderness in a patient over 3 weeks is highly suggestive of Giant Cell Arteritis. Immediate high-dose corticosteroids are indicated to prevent permanent blindness while we await the ESR and temporal artery biopsy results to confirm the diagnosis.
